confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion through its final reference and checked the relevant PDF pages, including Figure 12 and Table 2; the PDF has 29 pages and ends with references, with no appended supplement (PDF pp. 25-29).

The source is arXiv:2502.09577v2 dated 12 Aug 2025, in journal formatting bearing November 2025 publication information; the title and four listed authors match the form (PDF p. 1, title, authors, arXiv stamp and footer; p. 2, ACM reference format).

S1 is a formative study of 10 students recruited by snowball sampling, using the GPT-3 playground with pen-and-paper story planning; the reported analysis is thematic, with no randomized comparison or scored creativity outcome (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3-3.3).

An earlier system pilot is mentioned, but its sample size, allocation and creativity scores are not reported; the form appropriately leaves these unknown (PDF p. 14, Section 6.2.1; p. 16, Section 6.4).

The main evaluation recruited 10 people, described as 4 male and 6 female, mainly from local universities; final-results usage is reported for all 10 and Table 2 lists V1-V10 (PDF p. 17, Section 7.1; p. 20, Section 7.3.3; p. 21, Table 2).
The same participants used both Polymind and GPT-4 & Canvas; the two arm counts therefore refer to the same people, and no randomized-participant count is stated (PDF p. 18, Sections 7.2.2-7.2.3).

The paper states a Latin square to balance prompts and system conditions, but does not state random assignment to sequences or randomized condition order; design_class other and criterion_1 unclear are supported, and no randomized people study is confirmed (PDF p. 18, Section 7.2.2).

Polymind uses a GPT-4 backend and six predefined microtasks; the comparator combines ChatGPT-4 with the canvas and disables microtasking. Each ideation or outlining session lasts 12 minutes, with four sessions across both systems (PDF p. 16, Section 6.4; p. 18, Sections 7.2.2-7.2.3).

Two expert writers scored the outlines using TTCW; the reported values are 5.7 tests passed for GPT-4 & Canvas and 4 for Polymind, P = 0.23. Figure 12 labels the bars 5.7 and 4.0, respectively; the statistical test and aggregation across raters are not specified (PDF p. 18, Section 7.2.3; p. 20, Section 7.3.2 and Figure 12).

The idea-count statistics are Polymind median = 3, stdev = 1.06, and baseline median = 3, stdev = 8.51; 8.51 is printed in the PDF, and no p-value is supplied for this comparison (PDF p. 20, Section 7.3.2, opening paragraph).

Both reported strings and the one-line finding reproduce the PDF numbers correctly; the scored outcomes are outline creativity and idea fluency, whereas CSI responses concern perceived creativity support (PDF p. 18, Section 7.2.3; pp. 19-20, Section 7.3.2 and Figure 12).

Core exclusion is supported by the 10-person evaluation, below the codebook threshold of 50, despite output scoring. Context_class none is consistent with an AI-versus-AI system evaluation with unresolved randomization, rather than an AI-versus-human output dataset, an observational AI-adoption comparison, or a synthesis (PDF pp. 17-18, Sections 7.1-7.2.3; p. 20, Section 7.3.2).
summary: The source version, participant counts, design classifications, and reported results match the PDF. The main evaluation has 10 people using both AI systems, with Latin-square counterbalancing but no stated randomization, so no randomized people study is confirmed and the 50-person criterion is not met.
